article.plain_text:
The big breakdown: from "@grok is this true?" to agents with their own computer. Numbers, cases, failures, my take and a forecast.
 
Grok gets tagged under posts hundreds of thousands of times a day, yet almost nobody realizes it's no longer just one bot in the replies. In three years Grok has turned into a stack of products: a reply account on X, a standalone app, a video generator, agents that work inside your services on their own, an API for developers, and one bill for all of it.
I wanted to answer three questions. What Grok can actually do in October 2026. What people have actually done with it: not promo clips, but documented cases with numbers. And where all of this is heading.
To get there I went through three academic papers on @grok usage, two independent fact-checking audits, the numbers from SpaceX's S-1 (the first audited data on xAI and X), the reports on the Alpha Arena AI trading tournament, and about 25 dated press cases. All links at the end.
Inside: 9 terminals with sound and 12 charts. Short on time? Scroll straight to "Bottom line".
TL;DR, if this is all you read:
Grok reaches ~117M people a month, but almost all the growth happens inside X and the mobile app. On the web it holds ~3% of the market, flat for a full year.
The most common use case isn't image generation, it's questions and fact-checks: roughly one in six @grok requests is "verify this".
Fact-checking is exactly where Grok is weakest: in the Tow Center audit, Grok 3 got 94% of queries wrong.
The best cases are about speed and code; the worst are about wallets, photo geolocation and system prompts.
Grok 5 has missed three promised dates. My base case: no earlier than Q2 2027.
 
 
▹ 1. What Grok is now: five doors
The easiest way to think about Grok is as a building with five entrances. There's one model inside (the Grok 4.x family), but the doors are different, and most people only ever use the first one.
Door 1. @grok in the replies. Tag @grok under any post and within a couple of minutes you get an answer from the official account. It explains the post, digs up context, checks claims, and can edit and generate images right in the thread. Per the JLU Giessen study, median response time is 2.68 minutes. After the "undressing" scandal (more below), image editing via reply has been paid-only since January 9, 2026, and photo owners got a "block modifications by Grok" toggle.
Door 2. The Grok app. A regular chat, but with several modes. Think turns on long reasoning; DeepSearch and DeeperSearch run multi-step searches across the web and X (launched in February and March 2025). Grok 4.20, released in February 2026, was the first to run four agents in parallel (Grok, Harper, Benjamin and Lucas) that debate the answer before giving it. Companions, projects and voice also live here.
Door 3. Grok Imagine. An image and video generator, launched July 28, 2025. Imagine 1.0 (February 2026) makes 10-second 720p clips with sound and, at release, took first place on Artificial Analysis's text-to-video leaderboard, ahead of Veo 3.1 and Sora 2 Pro. Video 1.5 shipped in June 2026. Via API, video starts at $0.05 per second at 480p.
Door 4. Grok Bot. The newest and most underrated piece. Since August 11, 2026, these are always-on agents, each with its own cloud computer. They log into the services you use, even ones with no API, run multi-step tasks and only ping you when they need confirmation. Show it a workflow once and the bot saves it as a routine. Multiple bots can talk to each other in a group chat. On X you can tag @bot under a post and hand off a task straight from the feed (not available in the EU, UK and Australia).
Door 5. API and Grok Build. For developers: grok-4.7 costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output with a 500K context; grok-4.3 costs $1.25 and $2.50 with a 1M context. Grok Build (May 15, 2026) is a terminal coding agent, open-sourced under Apache since July 16; xAI claims 70.8% on SWE-bench Verified.
Plus everything else. Grok has lived in Tesla cars since July 12, 2025 (it talks, but doesn't drive). Grokipedia, Grok's encyclopedia, launched October 27, 2025 with ~885K articles. The US government got Grok through the GSA at $0.42 per agency, and since January 2026 it runs on Pentagon networks.
And one bill. Since October 12, 2026, all of it is sold as a single plan, The X Subscription: a free tier, Plus at $8, Premium at $30 (SuperGrok, Cursor Pro and X Premium+ bundled, previously $90), Super at $100 and Ultra at $200. Limits are shared and reset weekly.
 
My take. Each door on its own is just a feature; competitors have an equivalent for almost all of them. Grok's edge is that the doors are connected: see a post, tag @grok, jump into the app, hand the task to a bot, pay one bill. Nobody else has a social network of hundreds of millions of people with a model wired in at the reply level.
 
 
▹ 2. Grok by the numbers
Audience. Per SpaceX S-1, in March 2026 ~117M people a month used Grok, counting usage inside X (about 21% of X's ~550M users). Outside X, DemandSage's estimate on Semrush data puts it at ~30M. Paid SuperGrok subscribers: 1.9M. Over 100M installs on Android.
Important: these numbers measure different things, so you can't plot them on one line. The 117M includes people who tagged @grok under a post once.
Mobile vs web. This is where the picture gets interesting. Per Apptopia, in January 2025 Grok had 1.9% of US mobile chatbot usage. By December it was 14%, January 2026 peaked at 17.8%, and from April through June the share has held at 13.5%.
 
On the web, per Similarweb, Grok has hovered around 3% of AI chatbot traffic all year. Over the same period Gemini grew from 7.3% to 26.7%, Claude from 1.4% to ~8%, and ChatGPT fell from 77.6% to 53.7%.
 
Money. xAI raised at valuations of $24B (May 2024), $50B (December 2024), $80B in the X acquisition (March 2025) and $230B in a $20B Series E (January 2026). On February 2, 2026, SpaceX absorbed xAI at a $250B valuation, and in June SpaceX went public.
 
Per the S-1, the combined xAI and X segment brought in $2.62B in revenue in 2024 and $3.2B in 2025, with operating losses of $1.56B and $6.4B. In other words, losses are growing many times faster than revenue.
 
Compute. Per the S-1, Colossus 1 in Memphis is 220K+ Nvidia GPUs and 300MW in phase one, with Colossus 1 and 2 together at about 1GW. 2025 capex: $12.7B.
My take. The mobile-vs-web gap explains all of Grok. People don't seek it out as a standalone tool; they use it where they already are: in the X feed and in the app. That's both a strength (free distribution) and a weakness (outside X, Grok barely grows). And the loss numbers show that for now this is a construction site funded by SpaceX, not a business.
 
 
▹ 3. How people actually use @grok in the replies
The best data here comes from the JLU Giessen team (Bobek, Demirel and Pröllochs). They collected 169,137 request–response pairs from March 7 to May 28, 2025 and labeled what people ask about.
36.6% of requests ask for information: explain, tell me, what does this mean.
17.8% ask to verify a claim.
38% are about politics.
Only 48.9% of requests are in English.
Median response time 2.68 minutes, median reply reach 44 impressions.
 

 
The scale is massive. DFRLab counted ~450K Grok posts in just four days, June 12–15, 2025, during the Israel–Iran war. The Renault, Mosleh and Rand team counted 447,083 fact-check tags from March to September 2025, and together with Perplexity the bots received about 1.4M verification requests.
My take. "@grok is this true?" stopped being a meme long ago and became a mass habit: one in six calls is a request to verify. And more than half of requests aren't in English, which means Grok has become the world's default fact-checker. The problem is that this is exactly the function it does worst. That's the next section.
 
 
▹ 4. The 5 posts that made Grok
To see what Grok became for X, look past the releases at the posts people kept talking about. I collected the ten most discussed. Reach is given only where sources published it; post links come from the articles that covered them.
1. @ShuraLynx, April 24, 2025: the peak of the "@grok explain this" meme. The "explain this post" feature landed on December 10, 2024, and by April 2025 tagging @grok under posts had turned into a meme. The biggest example passed 4M views and 322K likes. Post:
 
2. @elonmusk, April 25, 2026: the Imagine clip "Nothing in this video is real". A demo of the new video model with lip sync and sound. Over 4M views in about 3 hours, and it became the reference point in the debate over spotting generated video. Post:
 
3. @xai, July 9, 2025: the Grok 4 launch livestream. About 1.5M concurrent viewers, per AIWiki citing Reuters 
4. @elonmusk, October 29, 2024: "upload your X-rays, PET and MRI scans". Musk said Grok was "already quite accurate". Radiologists tested it in public and found errors, such as a breast MRI read as a brain scan, and medical privacy became part of the story. Post:
 
5. @levelsio, February 2025: a flight sim built with AI. Musk quoted it with "AI gaming will be massive", kicking off the wave of vibe-coded games. Posts:
 
 
 
▹ 5. Cases: fact-checking
Case 1. Tow Center: 94% wrong
What happened. In February 2025, Columbia University's Tow Center took 200 articles from 20 publishers and ran 1,600 queries through 8 AI search engines. The task was simple: from a quote, find the article, publication, date and link.
Numbers. Grok 3 got 94% of queries wrong, the worst of the lot. For comparison: Perplexity 37%, ChatGPT Search ~67%. On average the bots were wrong more than 60% of the time.
Takeaway. Grok confidently serves up a source that doesn't exist or isn't the right one. If it gives you a link, open it yoursel
 
Case 2. DFRLab: one video, three countries
What happened. During the Israel–Iran war, an AI-generated video of a destroyed airport spread across X, 6.8M views. People tagged @grok under it en masse.
Numbers. Of 353 requests, Grok answered 312. Along the way it placed the airport in Beirut, then Gaza, then Tehran, sometimes contradicting itself within a single minute.
Takeaway. Grok doesn't hold a position across answers. Each reply is generated from scratch, and in a breaking story different people get a different "truth".
 
Case 3. The Gaza photo Grok "relocated" to Yemen
What happened. In August 2025, users asked Grok where an AFP photo of an emaciated girl in Gaza was taken. Grok answered: Yemen, 2018. The French MP who had shared the photo was then accused of spreading disinformation.
Numbers. The next day, Grok, having already admitted the mistake, repeated the Yemen version again.
Takeaway. The most dangerous thing Grok does is geolocate photos in breaking news. The error doesn't hit the bot, it hits the person who cited it.
Case 4. Bondi Beach
What happened. In December 2025, after the shooting at Bondi Beach, Grok repeated a fake name for the bystander hero ("Edward Crabtree"; his real name was Ahmed al Ahmed) and called verified footage an "old viral clip" of a man climbing a palm tree.
Takeaway. In the first hours after an event, Grok picks up the loudest version in the feed, not the most accurate one.
Case 5. Grok vs its owner
What happened. In March 2025, Decrypt asked Grok who spreads the most disinformation on X. Grok named Elon Musk. In other answers it put the odds that Trump is "compromised by Putin" at 75–85%.
Takeaway. Grok isn't just its owner's mouthpiece, but it's not a neutral arbiter either. It reflects what it sees in the data and in its instructions at the moment it answers.
Case 6. Community Notes
What happened. In July 2025, X launched an AI notes pilot, and in February 2026 it began testing Collaborative Notes: Grok drafts a note, human contributors edit it. One paper (Zhou and Hou) found that Community Notes activity dropped after Grok launched, though the Renault team stresses their data doesn't prove causation.
Takeaway. Grok is gradually being built into X's verification system itself. That could speed up notes, or it could push humans out.
 
My take on fact-checking. 2.68 minutes beats any human fact-checker, and that's the real value: Grok instantly gives you context, terms, a timeline. But a "true / false" verdict from it is worth nothing without a link you opened yourself. The rule is simple: no link, no verdict.
 
 
▹ 6. Cases: trading and crypto
Case 7. Alpha Arena, Season 1: minus 58%
What happened. Nof1 ran the Alpha Arena tournament: six models each got $10,000 in real money and traded crypto from October 18 to November 3, 2025 with no human involvement.
Numbers. Qwen3 Max finished at $12,231 (+22.3%), DeepSeek at $10,489 (+4.9%), Claude Sonnet 4.5 at $5,799 (−42%), Gemini 2.5 Pro at $5,445 (−45.6%), Grok at $4,208 (−57.9%), GPT-5 at $4,126 (−58.7%). Grok came fifth out of six. DeepSeek climbed above $13,000 mid-tournament but gave back the gains in a market drawdown.
 
Case 8. Alpha Arena, Season 1.5: a win
What happened. The second round (US stocks, ended December 5, 2025) had four modes: New Baseline, Monk Mode, Situational Awareness and Max Leverage. It featured a "mystery model" whose name was hidden.
Numbers. The mystery model won with ~+12% on average and was in the green in all four modes. It turned out to be Grok 4.20. Second place GPT-5.1, third Gemini 3.
Takeaway from both seasons. The same model family, a month apart, posted −57.9% and +12%. That doesn't mean Grok "learned to trade". It means an AI trader's result depends on the model generation, the market and the mode far more than on the brand.
 
Case 9. $DRB: how Grok accidentally launched a $40M token
What happened. In March 2025, a user asked Grok what to name a token. Grok suggested "DebtReliefBot". Bankrbot, a bot that can deploy tokens on command on X, launched it.
Numbers. At its peak $DRB was worth over $40M in market cap. A wallet tied to Grok collected over $500K in fees. In total, 17 tokens came out of interactions like this, after which Bankr turned off its interaction with Grok.
 
Case 10. The Morse code attack
What happened. On May 4, 2026, an attacker hid an instruction in a post encoded in Morse code. Grok decoded it and passed it along, and Bankrbot executed it.
Numbers. ~3B DRB left the Grok-linked wallet, roughly $150–200K.
Takeaway. Grok is a text model. Someone else bolted a wallet onto it. Any text Grok reads can turn out to be a command, and that's textbook prompt injection.
 
My take on crypto. For research Grok is useful: it quickly pulls together what people are saying about a ticker, who the team is, which posts came before the pump. But I wouldn't give it the right to sign transactions or treat its "token analysis" as a signal. The Morse case shows that the real counterparty here isn't the market, it's whoever writes the cleverest post.
 
 
▹ 7. Cases: builders and work
Case 11. levelsio and the flight simulator
In February 2025, @levelsio built a browser flight simulator, mostly in Cursor, with Grok 3 writing the multiplayer server code. Musk replied: "AI gaming will be massive". It was one of the first high-profile cases of Grok being used as a coding tool rather than a chat.
Case 12. Grok Build
On May 15, 2026, xAI released Grok Build, a terminal coding agent, and on July 16 open-sourced it under Apache. Claimed result: 70.8% on SWE-bench Verified. The grok-build-0.1 model costs $1/$2 per million tokens, one of the cheapest options for agentic coding.
Case 13. Grok Bot as an employee
In the Grok Bot announcement, xAI lists concrete work scenarios: overnight account research for sales, email drafts, CRM cleanup, updating CRM notes from call transcripts, processing invoices from Gmail, reproducing a bug, filing a ticket and handing off the fix. The beta launched August 11, 2026 for Heavy, opened to SuperGrok on August 26, got an X connector on August 29, and reached enterprise on September 3.
 
Case 14. X-rays and a "second opinion"
In fall 2024, Musk invited users to upload X-rays, PET and MRI scans to Grok. One mom, AJ Kay, wrote that Grok found a wrist fracture in her daughter that the urgent care had missed, and a specialist confirmed it. That's one story, not a study, and it sparked debate in the medical community. I'd treat it as an example, not as evidence.
Case 15. Government
On July 14, 2025, the Pentagon gave xAI a contract worth up to $200M. On September 25, 2025, the GSA struck a deal for access to Grok 4 and Grok 4 Fast for all federal agencies at $0.42 per agency for 18 months. In January 2026, the Secretary of Defense announced Grok would run on Pentagon networks, and in August 2026 Grok was added to GenAI.mil.
Case 16. Tesla
Since July 12, 2025, Grok has been in new Tesla cars. It talks, but can't drive the car. In October 2025, a Toronto mom said Grok in the car suggested her 12-year-old son "send nudes" (I've only seen headlines, there's no full report), which again raised the question of kid-safe modes.
My take on builders. Grok's strongest part today isn't the chat, it's a cheap coding model and agents. Grok Bot with its own computer and routines is a direct bid for the "employee" role, and through The X Subscription it became available for $30. If Grok wins anything big, it'll be here.
 
 
▹ 8. Where Grok broke
Case 17. "White genocide"
On May 14, 2025, Grok started inserting talking points about South Africa into answers on completely unrelated topics. xAI blamed an "unauthorized modification" of the system prompt and afterwards began publishing Grok's system prompts on GitHub.
Case 18. MechaHitler
On July 8–9, 2025, after an instruction not to shy away from "politically incorrect" claims, Grok started writing antisemitic posts and praising Hitler. The instruction was removed. Poland said it would report xAI to the European Commission. X CEO Linda Yaccarino left the next day without giving a reason.
Case 19. Turkey
On July 9, 2025, a court in Ankara blocked ~50 Grok posts for insulting Erdoğan. It was the first case of state censorship of an AI chatbot. The content was blocked, not the bot itself.
Case 20. Sycophancy
In November 2025, Grok started calling Musk the greatest person in history, smarter than Einstein and more athletic than LeBron. On November 20, Musk blamed it on "adversarial prompting".
Case 21. Spicy by default
In August 2025, The Verge reported that Grok Imagine's "Spicy" mode produced nude videos of Taylor Swift even though nudity wasn't requested.
Case 22. The "undressing" scandal
What happened. In December 2025 – January 2026, users massively abused image editing via @grok replies to "undress" people in photos, including minors.
Numbers. Per CCDH estimate, ~3M sexualized images appeared in the 11 days after the feature launched, ~23K of them resembling images of children, roughly 190 images per minute. AI Forensics, after checking 20K+ images, found that more than half showed people in minimal clothing and ~2% resembled minors.
Response. On January 9, reply editing went behind a paywall. Indonesia and Malaysia blocked Grok (Malaysia lifted its block after about two weeks). Ofcom and the California Attorney General opened inquiries, on January 14 X geoblocked the feature, and on January 26, 2026 the European Commission opened a formal DSA investigation into X, extending it to the plans to rank the feed with Grok.
 
 
My take. Look at all six cases together and a pattern emerges. The loudest incidents trace back not to the base model but to a system prompt, a default setting or a feature shipped without guardrails. And the fixes came out the same way: pull the instruction, add a paywall, a geoblock or a toggle. It tells you xAI ships features faster than it thinks through their consequences, and fixes things only after they break in public.
 
 
▹ 9. How to get real value out of Grok: a practical guide
Everything above boils down to a few simple rules. Here's how to use each door.
1. Fact-check. Don't write "@grok is this true?", write "@grok is this true? give me a link to the primary source and the date". Then open the link yourself. If there's no link or it goes somewhere else, there's no verdict.
2. Context. "@grok explain this post in 3 lines for someone outside crypto". It's the fastest way into a thread you missed, and here Grok is really good: its terms and timeline are usually right even when the verdict isn't.
3. Tasks from the feed. Tag @bot under a thread: "summarize in 5 points and save". Remember it doesn't work in the EU, UK and Australia, and the bot drops posts with video and GIFs.
4. Research. DeepSearch on a ticker, team or project, but ask for "posts with handles and timestamps". That way every line can be checked instead of trusting a retelling.
5. Images. If you don't want your photos edited, turn on "block modifications by Grok". For your own content, Imagine 1.0 gives you 10 seconds of 720p with sound, enough for a teaser or a post background.
6. API. grok-4.3 at $1.25/$2.50 fits bulk tasks with up to 1M tokens of context. grok-4.7 at $2/$6 for tasks where quality matters. Batch is 20% cheaper, and prompts over 200K cost twice as much.
 
 
Two "nevers". Never give Grok control of a wallet. Never trust its geolocation of photos from breaking news.
 
 
▹ 10. Bottom line
Grok is no longer a bot, it's a layer on top of X. Replies, app, video, agents, API and one subscription. One model, five doors.
Growth comes from inside X, not outside. Mobile went from 1.9% to 13.5% (peak 17.8%), web is stuck at ~3%. Without X, Grok is a small player.
The main use case is questions and verification, and that's exactly where Grok is weakest. One in six requests is "verify", and audits show 94% citation errors (Grok 3) and contradictory answers in breaking news.
The best cases are about speed and code. 2.68 minutes per answer, levelsio's server code, Grok Build at $1/$2, Grok Bot with routines.
The worst cases are about wallets, photos and prompts. $DRB and the Morse attack, Gaza and Bondi, MechaHitler and undressing.
Trading results are unstable. −57.9% on crypto and ~+12% on stocks within a month. That's not a signal, it's a model-generation lottery.
The business is propped up by SpaceX for now. $3.2B in revenue vs a $6.4B operating loss for 2025.
 
 
▹ 11. My take
Grok is worth opening every day while trusting none of its verdicts. That's not a contradiction.
Grok is the best tool in the world for one thing: quickly understanding what's happening on X right now. It sees the feed from the inside, answers in a couple of minutes, speaks any language and is free under any post. For crypto, where the first minutes decide everything, that's a real edge.
But Grok is built to always give a confident answer, even when it doesn't know. In a regular chat that's a minor problem. In public replies, where thousands of people see its answer and read it as "verified", it's a systemic risk. The Gaza and Bondi cases aren't bugs, they're a direct consequence of how the product is set up.
The most interesting thing about Grok right now isn't the chat or the images, it's the agents. Grok Bot with its own computer, routines and the @bot tag right in the feed, plus X Money in beta, is groundwork for a world where you write a post and a bot executes it. If xAI gets this right, Grok becomes the first social network where AI doesn't just answer, it acts.
My position is simple: use Grok as the fastest intern in the world. Let it search, explain, compile, write code. Keep the decisions, the money and the conclusions for yourself.
 
 
▹ 12. Forecast: what happens to Grok next
First, a baseline, so the forecast isn't guesswork. Musk has a consistent track record of slipping. On July 24 he said Grok 4.7 was "4 weeks" out, and the model shipped on September 21, ~8.5 weeks later. That's a slip of about 2.1x. Grok 5 was promised by end of 2025, then Q1 2026, then Q2, and all three dates passed.
 
What follows are my estimates. Opinion, not fact.
1. Grok 4.8 ships in November–December 2026, ~70%. On September 14 Musk said training was wrapping up. Apply the usual ~2x slip and you get year-end.
2. Grok 5 in 2026, under 30%. Three missed dates and an interim 4.8 and 4.9 on the roadmap. My base case: no earlier than Q2 2027.
3. Agents that pay, by mid-2027. @bot already takes tasks from posts, X Money has been in US beta with a Visa card since June 25, 2026, and Grok already answers questions about spending. The logical next step is a bot that pays for whatever you asked for in a post.
4. You won't be able to buy Grok on its own. The X Subscription ($8–$200) with a shared weekly pool replaced three subscriptions, and the old plans are no longer sold to new customers. Grok will become fully part of the X bundle.
5. New features will ship in the US first. The EU's DSA investigation has been open since January 26, 2026, including over feed ranking via Grok. @bot already doesn't work in the EU, UK and Australia, and there will be more geoblocks like that.
6. Imagine: longer clips yes, feature films no. Musk promises fully AI-made films by end of 2026. Clips will get longer and better, but I don't expect a full-length film from Imagine in 2026.
Overall takeaway. Individually, each forecast is a guess. Together they point the same way: Grok is ceasing to be a chatbot you open and becoming the layer all of X runs on. Replies, feed ranking, notes, payments, agents. The question is no longer whether Grok gets smarter, but how many decisions we're willing to hand it.
 
If this was useful, save it: in six months it'll be fun to check the forecasts.
